activate.note: Enable the hook for your shell. Fish, Nushell, and PowerShell use different activation syntax; follow the shell guide for those commands.
activate.commands:
eval "$(fnox activate bash)"
# Zsh:
eval "$(fnox activate zsh)"

deactivate.note: After shell activation, the fnox shell function applies this command to the current session. Remove the activation line from your startup file to disable it in future shells.

check.note: By default, check validates required secrets. Use --all to also check secrets whose missing-value policy is warn or ignore. The command validates resolution without printing resolved values.

completion.note: Generate completions for the named shell. Install or source the output according to that shell’s completion setup; generating it alone does not change your shell.
completion.commands:
fnox completion bash > fnox.bash
fnox completion zsh > _fnox

config-files.note: Inspect the effective file stack before debugging an unexpected value. An explicit config path skips directory discovery and adjacent local overrides; the global config still loads.
config-files.commands:
fnox config-files
fnox --profile staging config-files
fnox -c ./fnox.toml config-files

doctor.note: Check the local fnox setup, then test a specific provider or resolve all configured secrets to narrow down a failure.
doctor.commands:
fnox doctor
fnox provider test op
fnox check --all

edit.note: Open configuration in your editor. Configure EDITOR (or VISUAL) first. Use fnox set for an individual value so the selected provider handles storage.

exec.note: Put fnox options before --. Arguments after -- belong to the child command. To expand an injected variable in a shell expression, defer expansion to a child shell with single quotes.
exec.commands:
fnox exec -- npm start
fnox exec --profile production --if-missing error -- ./deploy.sh
fnox exec -- sh -c 'test -n "$DATABASE_URL"'

export.note: Exports contain real resolved values. JSON, YAML, and TOML wrap them in a secrets object; see the import/export guide before migrating. By default, export follows shell injection settings; `--all` also includes exec-only and non-injected secrets. `--dry-run` only suppresses a file write when `--output` is supplied: output to stdout still contains values.
export.commands:
fnox export --format json
# Create a private plaintext file (POSIX shell)
umask 077
fnox export --output .env

get.note: Print one resolved value to stdout. Use check --all when you only need to verify access without displaying the secret.
get.commands:
fnox get DATABASE_URL
fnox get DATABASE_URL --profile staging

import.note: Configure an encryption provider first. Remote storage providers are not import targets. When stdin carries the import data, use --force because stdin cannot also answer the confirmation prompt.
import.commands:
fnox import --input .env --provider age --dry-run
fnox import --input .env --provider age
cat secrets.json | fnox import json --provider age --force

init.note: In a terminal, the wizard can configure a provider and select it as the default. --skip-wizard creates a minimal config; it does not enable encryption. Configure a provider before storing sensitive values.

list.note: Lists the secrets configured in fnox. It does not enumerate every remote vault item. Values are hidden unless you request --values.
list.commands:
fnox list
fnox list --sources
fnox list --profile production

mcp.note: Run a stdio MCP server from the project directory. Configure its secret allowlist and authenticate to providers before starting the client.

profiles.note: Inspect the available profile names before selecting or composing them. Use --write-profile when writing with multiple active profiles.

provider.note: Manage configured provider instances. The instance name, such as op, is distinct from the provider type, such as 1password.
provider.commands:
fnox provider list
fnox provider test op

provider/add.note: Creates a provider configuration. Some types require interactive setup; others create placeholders that you must replace before use. For this command, the aws and gcp choices correspond to the aws-sm and gcp-sm config types.
provider/add.commands:
fnox provider add op 1password
fnox provider add sync-age age --global

provider/list.note: List configured provider instances for the selected profile. To find the supported provider types, use the provider catalog.
provider/list.commands:
fnox provider list
fnox --profile production provider list

provider/remove.note: Remove a provider definition from the configuration. Update secrets that reference it before removing it; this command does not delete the remote vault or its items.

provider/test.note: Use a configured instance name, not its type. A successful connection test does not guarantee that every referenced item exists; check --all validates those references too.
provider/test.commands:
fnox provider test op
fnox provider test --all
fnox check --all

reencrypt.note: After changing recipients, re-encrypt with an identity that can still decrypt the existing ciphertext. Repeat for each affected profile. This changes the encryption, not the underlying secret value.
reencrypt.commands:
fnox reencrypt --provider age --dry-run
fnox reencrypt --provider age
fnox reencrypt --provider age --profile staging

remove.note: Remove a secret definition from fnox configuration. The command does not delete or revoke the original value in a remote provider.
remove.commands:
fnox remove OLD_TOKEN --dry-run
fnox remove OLD_TOKEN

scan.note: Scan files for potential secrets using heuristics. Findings need review; a clean scan does not prove that files or git history contain no secrets.
scan.commands:
fnox scan .
fnox scan . --format json
fnox scan . --ignore "vendor/**"

set.note: Configure a provider first. Omitting VALUE prompts with hidden input in a terminal or reads piped stdin. Without a selected provider, set writes a plaintext default. --from-file preserves file contents, including trailing newlines.
set.commands:
fnox set DATABASE_URL --provider age
fnox set SSH_PRIVATE_KEY --provider age --from-file ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
fnox set DATABASE_URL --profile staging --provider age

sponsors.note: Show project sponsors in the terminal.

sync.note: Use a configured encryption provider as the target. --local-file writes a personal cache next to the project config; add that file to .gitignore. Run sync again after source values change.
sync.commands:
fnox sync --provider sync-age --local-file --dry-run
fnox sync --provider sync-age --local-file
fnox sync --provider sync-age --local-file DATABASE_URL

tui.note: Browse and copy values in the terminal. Dashboard edits are held in memory only; use set or remove to persist changes.

version.note: Include the version when reporting a bug or comparing local and CI behavior.

daemon.note: The daemon is opt-in and caches resolved values in memory. Enable it in config or with FNOX_DAEMON=on to use it for supported reads.
daemon.commands:
fnox daemon status
fnox daemon start
FNOX_DAEMON=on fnox check --all

daemon/start.note: Start the per-user daemon. Enable daemon mode in configuration or the environment for subsequent reads to use it.
daemon/start.commands:
fnox daemon start
fnox daemon status

daemon/status.note: Inspect the current daemon state when diagnosing cache behavior.

daemon/clear.note: Clear cached values after changing a secret in its source provider. This clears running daemon caches; it does not remove encrypted sync caches.

daemon/stop.note: Stop the daemon and discard its in-memory cache. If daemon mode remains enabled, a later supported read may start it again.

lease.note: Create and manage temporary credentials from configured lease backends. fnox exec can create or reuse a lease automatically.
lease.commands:
fnox lease list --active
fnox exec -- aws s3 ls

lease/create.note: Create a lease for a configured backend. Without a backend name, all configured backends are selected. Output contains usable temporary credentials; avoid putting it in logs.
lease/create.commands:
fnox lease create aws --duration 30m
fnox lease create aws --interactive

lease/list.note: Inspect the local lease ledger. This is a record of leases tracked by fnox, not a complete inventory of credentials at the service.
lease/list.commands:
fnox lease list --active
fnox lease list --expired

lease/revoke.note: Use an ID from lease list. Remote revocation depends on the backend; native-expiry backends cannot invalidate a token immediately through fnox.
lease/revoke.commands:
fnox lease list --active
fnox lease revoke LEASE_ID

lease/cleanup.note: Ask backends to clean up expired tracked leases that require manual revocation. Backend credentials and network access may be needed.

proxy.note: Configure destination rules before launching a command. The proxy controls credential injection; it is not an operating-system sandbox.
proxy.commands:
fnox proxy rules
fnox proxy run -- node agent.js

proxy/rules.note: Inspect effective rules without resolving their secrets. Confirm domains, methods, and paths before launching the client.
proxy/rules.commands:
fnox proxy rules
fnox --profile staging proxy rules

proxy/run.note: The child receives placeholders and proxy/CA settings. Its HTTP client must honor those settings. Configure proxy rules before running this command.
